newsitem.title: GERMANY: More work needed on German '98 budget - sources.
newsitem.headline: More work needed on German '98 budget - sources.

text.p: More work is needed to finalise Germany's 1998 budget, but the amount that needs to be saved has been narrowed down to below 10 billion marks, sources in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition said on Tuesday.

Decisions on the 1998 budget, as well as a supplementary budget for 1997, are not expected until next week. Meanwhile, Finance Minister Theo Waigel will hold separate meetings with ministers, and more coalition talks are planned.

Kohl affirmed on Tuesday that Germany would hit the strict budget deficit target of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product to qualify for Europe's single currency. Tough savings will be needed to hit that figure, the sources said.
"No ministry will emerge completely unscathed," one said.

Waigel had started out with a forecast shortfall for 1998 of over 30 billion marks, arising from a weak tax take and high benefit payments to Germany's four million jobless. Much of that will covered by the sale of shares in Deutsche Telekom AG.
Sources in the three parties making up Kohl's centre-right coalition said negotiations were going well, with talks on the defence, transport and agriculture budgets already advanced.

However, the sources reported resistance to spending cuts from Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt, who is responsible for state aid to industry, and Labour Minister Norbert Bluem, who wants to defend his welfare budget from Waigel's red pen.
